source.title_on_document: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays

supplement.where: The paper refers to no supplementary material. Data availability (p. 29): the generated essays, extracted structural features, and analysis code 'will be made available upon publication'.

paper_design_summary: The authors take 1,375 student-written essays from the public AIDE Kaggle corpus (two topics) and use GPT-5-mini to rewrite each one under three prompts (Minimal 'improve', Structural, Delegative 'rewrite in your own way') and to write 1,375 AI-only essays, giving 6,875 essays in five conditions. GPT-5 scores every essay three times on five structural dimensions and holistic quality. The paper compares means and variances (variance ratio, Brown-Forsythe test, bootstrap CIs) between the human essays and each AI condition; no person used AI.

studies.label: AIDE essay corpus: human-only vs AI-only vs three LLM-rewrite conditions

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance. Each existing human essay was computationally rewritten under all three prompt strategies. The within structure refers to the matched human essays and their rewrites; the AI-only essays are a separately generated baseline.
assignment.quote: First, the H+AI conditions were generated computationally rather than through actual student–AI interaction.
assignment.locator: p. 11, Section 3.3, Condition H+AI; p. 15, Section 4.1; pp. 27-28, Section 5.4

arms.name: Human-only (H)
arms.description: Unmodified human-written AIDE essays; 1,375 analyzed essays in this condition (output count, not a people count; p. 10, Table 1; pp. 11-12, Section 3.3 and Table 2).

arms.name: AI-only (A)
arms.description: GPT-5-mini essays generated from the original topic instructions and source materials; 1,375 analyzed essays in this condition (output count, not a people count; p. 10, Table 1; pp. 11-12, Section 3.3 and Table 2).

arms.name: H+AI Minimal
arms.description: GPT-5-mini rewrites requesting improvement while retaining the topic and general direction; 1,375 analyzed essays in this condition (output count, not a people count; p. 10, Table 1; pp. 11-12, Section 3.3 and Table 2).

arms.name: H+AI Structural
arms.description: GPT-5-mini rewrites requesting stronger argument structure, counterarguments and rebuttals, and logical coherence while retaining the original perspective and main arguments; 1,375 analyzed essays in this condition (output count, not a people count; p. 10, Table 1; pp. 11-12, Section 3.3 and Table 2).

arms.name: H+AI Delegative
arms.description: GPT-5-mini rewrites on the same topic in the model's own way, permitting complete restructuring and rewriting; 1,375 analyzed essays in this condition (output count, not a people count; p. 10, Table 1; pp. 11-12, Section 3.3 and Table 2).

participants.who: No participants. Corpus of 6,875 essays: 1,375 student-written essays from the AIDE Kaggle dataset (Topic 0 'Car-free cities', 707; Topic 1 electoral college, 668; 3 AI-labeled AIDE essays excluded), 1,375 GPT-5-mini AI-only essays, and 1,375 GPT-5-mini rewrites of the human essays under each of three prompts (pp. 9-11, Table 1).
participants.quote: First, the H+AI conditions were generated computationally rather than through actual student–AI interaction.

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-5-mini (essay generation and rewriting, OpenAI API); GPT-5 as automated evaluator
ai_tool.how_used: Each human essay was sent to GPT-5-mini in a single API turn with one of three prompts: Minimal ('Please improve the following essay...'), Structural (strengthen argument structure, add counterarguments, improve coherence), Delegative ('rewrite it on the same topic in your own way'). AI-only essays were generated from the topic instructions and source materials (p. 11, Table 2).

task.description: Explanatory essay on limiting car usage and argumentative essay on the U.S. Electoral College (AIDE prompts with standardized instructions and source materials); scored by GPT-5 on argument depth, perspective plurality, abstract-concrete oscillation, cohesion architecture, structural originality (1-5), and holistic quality (1-6).

outcomes.name: Diversity of Cohesion Architecture scores across essays (variance ratio VR = var_H / var_H+AI; HI = 1 - var_H+AI / var_H)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Cohesion Architecture assesses the quality of logical connections between and within paragraphs on a 1-5 rubric scale. The analyzed essay score is the mean of three independent GPT-5 evaluations (p. 12, Table 3; p. 13, Section 3.4). Diversity is dispersion of these scores across essays within each condition, not embedding similarity. Cohesion homogenization occurs for both topics (p. 23, Table 12 and Section 4.6).

contrasts.treatment_arm: H+AI Minimal (GPT-5-mini rewrite, 'Please improve', n = 1,375 essays)
contrasts.reported: SD H 0.47 vs Minimal 0.22 (Table 5); Minimal VR 4.554 [95% CI 3.88, 5.45] (Table 7; VR > 1 = homogenization); HI +0.780 (Table 8). Structural VR 3.160 [2.72, 3.73], HI +0.684; Delegative VR 3.180 [2.81, 3.62], HI +0.686. Direction refers to diversity (lower variance in H+AI).
contrasts.locator: p. 10, Table 1; p. 16, Table 5; p. 17, Table 7; p. 19, Table 8

diversity_detail.metric: VR = variance(H) / variance(H+AI); HI = 1 - variance(H+AI) / variance(H). VR > 1 and HI > 0 indicate homogenization; VR < 1 and HI < 0 indicate diversification (p. 14, Section 3.6, equations 1-2).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: Not applicable: VR and HI use GPT-5 rubric scores, not embeddings.
diversity_detail.computed_over: Variance across essay scores within a condition. Each H+AI prompt condition rewrites the same 1,375 human source essays, and each rewrite-condition variance is compared with the human-only variance (p. 10, Table 1; p. 11, Section 3.3; p. 15, Section 4.1).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for VR using 10,000 resamples; Brown-Forsythe variance tests (p. 14, Section 3.6; p. 16, paragraph before Table 7). Human originals and rewrites share source essays; the bootstrap resampling unit and preservation of matching are not specified, and no participant-level uncertainty is reported.
diversity_detail.notes: Cohesion homogenization occurs for both topics (p. 23, Table 12 and Section 4.6). Contrast directions refer to diversity: higher means greater variance across essays.

outcomes.name: Diversity of Argument Depth scores across essays (VR and HI); prompt-dependent
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Argument Depth assesses the number of inferential layers between claims and evidence on a 1-5 rubric scale. The analyzed essay score is the mean of three independent GPT-5 evaluations (p. 12, Table 3; p. 13, Section 3.4). The Structural prompt diversifies Argument Depth while Minimal and Delegative homogenize it; this reversal holds for both topics (p. 23, Table 12 and Section 4.6).

outcomes.name: Holistic essay quality (GPT-5 score, 1-6)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-5 assigns holistic essay quality on a 1-6 scale, from very poor to excellent; the analyzed score is the mean of three independent evaluations of each essay (p. 12, Table 3; p. 13, Section 3.4). Mean quality is compared using Welch's t-test and reported Cohen's d (p. 14, Section 3.6; p. 16, Table 6). Quality improvement replicates for both topics (p. 23, Table 12 and Section 4.6).

contrasts.reported: H mean -> H+AI mean: Minimal 2.69 -> 4.55, Cohen's d 4.102; Structural 2.69 -> 4.23, d 3.754; Delegative 2.69 -> 4.74, d 4.814; p < 0.0001 for each of the three comparisons (Table 6, Welch t-test). Mean (SD): H 2.69 (0.47), A 4.34 (0.41), Minimal 4.55 (0.44), Structural 4.23 (0.35), Delegative 4.74 (0.38) (Table 5).

outcomes.name: Diversity of Abstract–Concrete Oscillation scores across essays (VR and HI)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Abstract-Concrete Oscillation assesses the frequency and purposefulness of transitions between abstract claims and concrete examples on a 1-5 rubric scale. The analyzed essay score is the mean of three independent GPT-5 evaluations (p. 12, Table 3; p. 13, Section 3.4). Diversity is dispersion of these scores across essays within each condition, not embedding similarity. The overall diversification reverses by topic: diversified for Topic 0 but homogenized for Topic 1 (p. 23, Table 12 and Section 4.6).

contrasts.reported: Mean (SD): H 2.84 (0.39), A 3.76 (0.35), Minimal 3.37 (0.45), Structural 3.53 (0.46), Delegative 3.37 (0.44) (Table 5). Minimal VR 0.737 [95% CI 0.66, 0.82], Structural VR 0.711 [0.63, 0.80], Delegative VR 0.761 [0.68, 0.85] (Table 7). HI -0.357 / -0.407 / -0.314 in Minimal / Structural / Delegative order (Table 8). Direction refers to higher across-essay variance in rewrites overall. Topic-stratified analyses show diversification for Topic 0 and homogenization for Topic 1 (Table 12).

eligibility.reason: No people were assigned to AI assistance: the H+AI outputs are computational single-turn rewrites of existing essays (pp. 11-12, Section 3.3; pp. 27-28, Section 5.4). The counts of 1,375 per condition and 6,875 overall are essays; the number of distinct people analyzed is not stated, so the at-least-50-people criterion is unclear (p. 10, Table 1; p. 15, Section 4.1). The output criterion is met because GPT-5 scores structural originality and holistic quality on the essay outputs and the paper compares across-essay score variances (pp. 12-14, Sections 3.4-3.6; pp. 16-19, Tables 5-8). Core remains no because random assignment of people to AI assistance is absent; this is AI-versus-human output context evidence.

one_line_finding: GPT-5-mini rewrites of 1,375 AIDE student essays scored higher on GPT-5-rated quality (2.69 to 4.55, d = 4.102 for the Minimal prompt, Table 6, p. 16) and were less varied in cohesion architecture (variance ratio 4.554 [3.88, 5.45], Table 7, p. 17; HI +0.68 to +0.78, Table 8, p. 19), but more varied in perspective plurality (VR 0.685 to 0.959), and the structural prompt diversified argument depth (VR 0.528, HI -0.894).
notes: data_and_code.data_url is the public AIDE source dataset, not a release of the generated study outputs. The generated essays, extracted structural features, and analysis code are promised upon publication; this version supplies no URL for those materials (p. 29, Data availability). Outcome n_units = 2,750 counts output observations in each named two-condition comparison, obtained by summing the two printed condition counts of 1,375 essays (p. 10, Table 1); the human essays and their rewrites share source essays, so this is not a count of independent people (p. 15, Section 4.1).
